plotting_plan.title: Three-Layer Editorial Competence Framework
plotting_plan.objective: Visual summary (Block Diagram) of the three-layer editorial competence framework: Layer 1 Mechanical (proofreading PUEBI/KBBI), Layer 2 Structural (TEEL+, transitions, depth model), Layer 3 Substantive (fact verification, style engine), with the layer-to-analogy mapping (bricklayer, architect, curator) from idea.md.

plotting_plan.title: Style Engine with Hybrid Weighting
plotting_plan.objective: Conceptual diagram (Flowchart) of the style engine: 5 base styles (Academic, Journalistic, Literary, Popular, Persuasive), hybrid mode with primary/secondary/tertiary weights 60/30/10, and the 7 micro parameters (formality 1-10, sentence length, technical density, analogy frequency, rhetorical questions, licentia poetica tolerance, narrative perspective) feeding the 7-stage workflow.

plotting_plan.title: Seven-Stage Editing Workflow
plotting_plan.objective: Visual summary (Flow Diagram) of the 7-stage workflow from idea.md: Intake & Diagnosis, Substantive Editing, Structural Editing, Sentence Editing, Proofreading, Enhancement, Output & Editor Notes, showing per-stage outputs including the 4 output modes and the 7-dimension quality score.

plotting_plan.title: Progressive Disclosure Context Cost
plotting_plan.objective: Visual summary (Bar Chart) comparing estimated token cost of the three progressive disclosure levels from experimental_log.md Section 2.5: discovery (~100 tokens, frontmatter), activation (<5000 tokens, SKILL.md body), execution (per-file references loaded on demand), illustrating why the 173-line core keeps context lean.

plotting_plan.title: Self-Reported Quality Scores on Worked Examples
plotting_plan.objective: Visual summary (Radar Chart) of the 7-dimension self-reported quality scores for worked examples 1 (academic-popular hybrid) and 3 (literary) from experimental_log.md Table 2.2, annotated with the self-assessment bias caveat and the absence of scores in Clean output mode.

plotting_plan.title: Verified Skill Artifact Characteristics
plotting_plan.objective: Visual summary (Bar Chart) of verified artifact characteristics from experimental_log.md Table 2.1: 173-line core SKILL.md, 1014/1024-character description, 6 reference files, 3 asset files, 9 project-level plus 8 global install paths, 0 validator warnings.

introduction_strategy.hook_hypothesis: LLM-based text editing is ad hoc and English-centric; Indonesian-language manuscripts lack structured editorial support spanning the mechanical, structural, and substantive layers, and the emerging SKILL.md portable skill format has not yet been evaluated for a real editorial domain skill.
introduction_strategy.problem_gap_hypothesis: No open, portable, skill-based editorial methodology for Indonesian exists that (i) formalizes PUEBI/KBBI rules for on-demand LLM loading, (ii) provides a style engine with hybrid styles and micro parameters, and (iii) reports measured artifact characteristics and a multi-runtime portability plan grounded in a verifiable experimental log.
search_directions: Find surveys and highly cited papers establishing the state and real-world impact of automatic grammar checking and text revision for low-resource languages, especially Indonesian (search window up to 2026-08-31 only)
Search for published surveys on LLM-based text editing, style transfer, and text simplification
Identify foundational papers that established statistical and neural grammatical error correction (GEC)

Find foundational documentation and papers establishing agent skills and the Model Context Protocol (Anthropic Agent Skills, Open Agent Skills / SKILL.md specification, MCP) as emerging portable instruction formats
Search for papers on prompt engineering and system-prompt design for LLM writing assistance and its evaluation protocols

related_work_strategy.overview: Investigate four distinct methodology clusters to build a research graph proving the necessity of a layered, PUEBI-grounded, portable editorial skill: automatic grammar checking & GEC, LLM-as-editor prompting, agent skill standards with progressive disclosure, and Indonesian language resources and editing tools.

subsections.subsection_title: 2.1 Automatic Grammar Checking and Grammatical Error Correction
subsections.methodology_cluster: Rule-based and neural grammatical error correction (GEC) systems
subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Identify current SOTA GEC systems and grammar checkers (e.g., LanguageTool, transformer-based GEC) up to 2026-08-31; determine their coverage of structural and substantive editing layers and their support for the Indonesian language.
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: These tools operate at the mechanical layer only (spelling and grammar); they cannot enforce PUEBI-specific conventions, style selection, coherence structure, or factual verification, and most are English-centric with limited Indonesian coverage.
limitation_search_queries: grammar error correction low-resource languages limitations coverage
grammar checker stylistic coherence structural coverage evaluation
Indonesian grammar checker PUEBI rule coverage accuracy
subsections.bridge_to_our_method: ENIP encodes the mechanical layer as a modular PUEBI/KBBI rule reference and extends editing to the structural layer (TEEL+, transitions, depth model) and substantive layer (fact-verification protocol, style engine).

subsections.methodology_cluster: Prompt-based text revision, style transfer, and editing instructions with LLMs
subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Identify current approaches using LLMs for text revision, style transfer, and editing up to 2026-08-31; determine their evaluation protocols, especially how self-assessment bias is handled.
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: Unguided or single-prompt LLM editing is ad hoc: no layered workflow, no PUEBI grounding, no transparent justification of significant changes, and quality is typically self-assessed without human editor validation.
limitation_search_queries: LLM text editing evaluation self-assessment bias human evaluation
style transfer Indonesian language LLM evaluation
subsections.bridge_to_our_method: ENIP provides a structured 7-stage workflow, a style engine with hybrid weighting, four output modes including Track Changes and Consultation, and a 7-dimension rubric designed for human editor validation.

subsections.subsection_title: 2.3 Agent Skills and Portable Instruction Formats
subsections.methodology_cluster: Agent skills, Model Context Protocol, and portable instruction formats (SKILL.md, AGENTS.md)
subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Identify the Open Agent Skills (SKILL.md) specification, Anthropic Agent Skills, MCP, and AGENTS.md ecosystem up to 2026-08-31; determine native SKILL.md reader support across runtimes and the progressive disclosure mechanics.
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: The skill ecosystem is young: no published evaluation of cross-runtime portability or context overhead for a real domain skill exists, and portable skills for Indonesian language editing are absent from public registries.
limitation_search_queries: agent skills SKILL.md open specification portability evaluation
progressive disclosure context overhead agent skills measurement
MCP agent skills standardization adoption survey
subsections.bridge_to_our_method: ENIP is a SKILL.md skill with verified artifact characteristics (experimental_log.md Table 2.1) and a planned 8-runtime portability study with a deterministic installer and validator.

subsections.subsection_title: 2.4 Indonesian Language Resources and Editing Tools
subsections.methodology_cluster: Indonesian language technology and editorial resources (KBBI, PUEBI, Indonesian NLP toolkits)
subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Identify Indonesian NLP resources and editing tools (KBBI dictionaries, Indonesian spell checkers, PUEBI-based tools, Indonesian NLP toolkits) up to 2026-08-31; determine their coverage and their integration difficulty into LLM workflows.
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: Existing Indonesian editing tools cover only the mechanical checking layer and are not structured for on-demand LLM loading; their rule representations are neither modular nor portable across agent runtimes.
limitation_search_queries: Indonesian NLP resources tools survey coverage
PUEBI spelling checker Indonesian tools evaluation
subsections.bridge_to_our_method: ENIP formalizes PUEBI/KBBI rules into a modular reference file (references/PUEBI.md) loaded on demand by the skill, with uncertainty marked explicitly instead of guessed.

content_bullets: State the problem: Indonesian manuscript editing lacks structured editorial support spanning mechanical, structural, and substantive layers.
Announce the contribution: ENIP, a portable SKILL.md skill encoding a three-layer editorial methodology with a PUEBI-grounded style engine and a 7-dimension quality protocol.
Summarize verified artifact characteristics from experimental_log.md Table 2.1 and the planned evaluation (baselines B1-B3, human editor validation, trigger reliability, context overhead).

Open with the editorial pain point for Indonesian manuscripts: mechanical errors are partially covered by spell checkers while structural and substantive issues are unaddressed (idea.md Problem Statement items 1-2).
Motivate the emerging SKILL.md portable skill format as the delivery vehicle, noting the absence of public portability evaluations for domain skills (idea.md Problem Statement item 4).
State the core hypothesis: a layered editorial skill outperforms unguided LLM editing and mechanical checkers while staying portable (idea.md Core Hypothesis).
List the four expected contributions from idea.md: layered competence formalization, Indonesian style engine, open PUEBI rule base, portability study and evaluation protocol.
Scope the paper strictly to the artifact and data in experimental_log.md; do not over-claim generalization beyond the 20-manuscript planned evaluation target.
